references.text: Describes the general rule for freeing Hebrew slaves after six years of service, which forms the context for verse 11 regarding release without payment.
The immediate context describing the three rights (food, clothing, and marital rights) that a master must provide to a female slave, which verse 11 refers to as 'these three things'.
A parallel law concerning the release of Hebrew slaves, which also mentions release without payment and requires the master to give gifts upon freeing them.
Uses the same expression 'חִנָּם' (without payment/free) in connection with letting a woman go free, as in Exodus 21:11.
Concerns the treatment of Israelite slaves and their release, related to the principle of release without ransom.
A prophetic condemnation of those who did not free their Hebrew slaves, highlighting the importance of the laws in Exodus 21 regarding release.
Nehemiah refers to the freeing of slaves and the buying and selling of Jewish brothers, linking back to the slave laws in Exodus.
Both verses illustrate the same legislative principle that physical injury to a slave triggers immediate freedom as compensation.
